items.title: Jon Stewart Strikes Two-Year Deal To Remain As ‘The Daily Show’ Host Through 2028
items.summary:
Jon Stewart has signed a new two-year deal to continue hosting and executive producing The Daily Show, keeping him at Comedy Central through the end of 2028. The agreement extends a run that had been set to lapse at the end of this year under a deal he signed in November 2025.

The timeline matters: the new contract carries Stewart through another general election cycle, the terrain the show has built its identity on. It also answers, at least for now, the question of whether Skydance would keep a political comedy franchise on the books after CBS canceled The Late Show with Stephen Colbert ahead of Skydance taking control of Paramount last year.

Deadline reported the deal, noting it is the first significant late-night move Skydance has made since closing its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, which installed George Cheeks as Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer of Skydance TV. The consolidation also puts Stewart back under the same corporate roof as John Oliver, his former Daily Show colleague, who recently signed a one-year extension running through the end of 2027.

Stewart's arrangement on the show remains unchanged. He hosts Monday nights, with Ronny Chieng, Josh Johnson, Jordan Klepper, Michael Kosta and Desi Lydic rotating through the rest of the week. He executive produces alongside showrunner Jen Flanz and his longtime manager James Dixon.

"Jon Stewart is a generational talent and The Daily Show continues to be one of the most influential franchises on television and a cornerstone of Comedy Central," Cheeks said. "We are excited to continue our partnership with Jon and his award-winning news team."

With the extension locked, Stewart's Monday-night post and the rotating-host structure stay in place at Comedy Central for two more years, and the show enters the next election cycle with its current lineup intact.

items.title: Charli XCX Brings Out Chappell Roan, PinkPantheress, & Adéla At The Forum, underscores Brings Out Jane Remover
items.summary:
Charli XCX played two nights at the Forum in Los Angeles over the weekend and used both of them to stack the stage with guests. The run produced four surprise appearances across the two shows, including one from the opening act's set.

Saturday brought the biggest name. Chappell Roan, who co-headlined Primavera with Charli in 2025, came out midway through the set to sing "Boom Clap," marking the first time the early-career single has turned up on this tour. PinkPantheress appeared later in the night to perform her own hit "Stateside," and the Dare joined Charli onstage for "Guess," the track he produced.

Sunday's guest was Adéla, this year's breakout pop arrival, who performed her biggest song, "Nicole Kidman." She wasn't the first unannounced performer of the evening, though. Opening act underscores brought out Jane Remover earlier in the night to debut an unreleased collaboration titled "Everything."

Stereogum reported on both nights, pointing to the pair's history together: underscores and Jane Remover previously worked on "Uncanny long arms" in 2023. The new song's debut at the Forum was its first public airing.

Footage from the weekend circulated on TikTok, which is where most of the documentation of the guest spots now lives. Charli's tour continues with the Forum dates behind it.

items.title: Gwyneth Paltrow To Star In ‘The Apology’ A24 Series Which Lands 2-Season Order At Netflix With Thomas Vinterberg Directing
items.summary:
Netflix has handed a two-season straight-to-series order to The Apology, a thriller drama starring Gwyneth Paltrow and directed by Thomas Vinterberg. The project comes from Cut To, the A24-based company run by producer Hipps, and marks Paltrow's first series regular role and Vinterberg's first time directing U.S. television.

Written by Joe Murtagh, who also serves as showrunner, the series follows Evelyn and Caleb Amspoker, whose son was murdered 18 years earlier in a cold case that drew national attention. A stranger surfaces and confesses, but when the couple learn the killer may receive a reduced sentence, they decide to handle the matter themselves. Murtagh, Vinterberg, Paltrow and Hipps all executive produce.

Deadline reported that Netflix bought the competitive package preemptively and that the streamer declined to comment. The order came from Jinny Howe, head of U.S. and Canada scripted series, who communicated with co-CEO Ted Sarandos on the decision; incoming Chief Content Officer Peter Rice, who officially started Monday, was not involved.

The timing lands in the middle of a turbulent stretch at the company. Netflix replaced Bela Bajaria with Rice last Thursday, cut film head Dan Lin over the weekend, and laid off roughly 1,000 people, all while Wall Street watches slowing engagement growth. The two-season commitment echoes the 2011 order for House of Cards, the move that first established Netflix as an originals player.

Cut To has become a reliable seller of A-list packages since launching two years ago, with straight-to-series orders including Discretion with Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning at Paramount+, Trigger Point with Joel Edgerton at Netflix, and a Jack Thorne espionage thriller starring Millie Bobby Brown and David Harbour, also at Netflix.

Paltrow previously did a recurring arc on Fox's Glee and recently appeared in the feature Marty Supreme. Murtagh created the 2023 series The Woman In the Wall. A24's broader television slate includes Hulu's The Spot, Peacock's Superfakes and Crystal Lake, which hit number one on Peacock after its October 15 launch.
